import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import re
import shutil
import stat
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest

class BoardP4mStartProductionParserTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Feed real host CLI JSON through the runner's production JSON checks."""

    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls._temporary = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="idma-p4m-parser-")
        cls.temp = Path(cls._temporary.name)
        include = cls.temp / "uapi"
        (include / "linux").mkdir(parents=True)
        shutil.copy2(ROOT / "linux/include/uapi/linux/idma.h", include / "linux/idma.h")
        compiler = os.environ.get("HOSTCC", "cc")
        flags = [compiler, "-std=c11", "-Wall", "-Wextra", "-Werror", "-O2", "-I", str(include)]
        cls.binary = cls.temp / "idma_experiment"
        cls.stub = cls.temp / "ioctl_stub.so"
        subprocess.run(flags + [str(ROOT / "bench/idma_experiment.c"), "-o", str(cls.binary)], check=True)
        subprocess.run(flags + ["-shared", "-fPIC", str(ROOT / "tests/experiment_cli_test_stub.c"), "-o", str(cls.stub)], check=True)
        cls.device = cls.temp / "device"
        cls.device.touch()
        cls.calls = cls.temp / "calls.log"
        cls.script_text = SCRIPT.read_text()
        cls.harness_prelude = cls._make_harness_prelude()
        cls.busybox_bin = cls.temp / "busybox-bin"
        cls.busybox_bin.mkdir()
        if BUSYBOX.is_file():
            awk = cls.busybox_bin / "awk"
            awk.write_text("#!/bin/sh\nexec %s awk \"$@\"\n" % BUSYBOX)
            awk.chmod(0o755)

    @classmethod
    def tearDownClass(cls):
        cls._temporary.cleanup()

    @classmethod
    def _make_harness_prelude(cls):
        names = ("unquote", "int_of", "json_get", "json_check", "check_case_json")
        parts = ["#!/bin/sh\n", "V_DID=10\nA_DID=11\nNO_AGGRESSOR=4294967295\n"]
        for name in names:
            parts.append(_extract_shell_function(cls.script_text, name))
        return "\n".join(parts)

    def _write_json(self, name, row):
        path = self.temp / name
        path.write_text(json.dumps(row) + "\n")
        return path

    def _run_cli(self, args):
        self.calls.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        env = os.environ.copy()
        env.update(LD_PRELOAD=str(self.stub), IDMA_TEST_MODE="ok", IDMA_TEST_LOG=str(self.calls))
        result = subprocess.run([str(self.binary), "--device", str(self.device), *args],
                                env=env, text=True, capture_output=True, check=False)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result)
        return json.loads(result.stdout)

    def _run_harness(self, call):
        harness = self.temp / "harness.sh"
        harness.write_text(self.harness_prelude + "\n" + call + "\n")
        env = os.environ.copy()
        if BUSYBOX.is_file():
            env["PATH"] = str(self.busybox_bin) + ":" + env.get("PATH", "")
            result = subprocess.run([str(BUSYBOX), "ash", str(harness)], env=env,
                                    text=True, capture_output=True, check=False)
        else:
            result = subprocess.run(["sh", str(harness)], env=env,
                                    text=True, capture_output=True, check=False)
        return result

    def test_checks_accept_real_batch_cli_json(self):
        row = self._run_cli(["--batch", "--aggressor", "1"])
        path = self._write_json("batch.json", row)
        result = self._run_harness('check_case_json case-batch "%s" batch 4096 11 0' % path)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)

    def test_checks_accept_real_p4m_solo_cli_json(self):
        row = self._run_cli(["--p4m"])
        path = self._write_json("p4m-solo.json", row)
        result = self._run_harness(
            'check_case_json case-p4m-solo "%s" p4m 4096 4294967295 1' % path)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)

    def test_checks_accept_real_p4m_pair_cli_json(self):
        row = self._run_cli(["--p4m", "--aggressor", "1"])
        path = self._write_json("p4m-pair.json", row)
        result = self._run_harness(
            'check_case_json case-p4m-pair "%s" p4m 4096 11 1' % path)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)

    def test_checks_reject_real_cli_json_after_mutation(self):
        row = self._run_cli(["--batch", "--aggressor", "1"])
        row["result"]["victim"]["data_errors"] = 1
        path = self._write_json("batch-bad.json", row)
        result = self._run_harness('check_case_json case-batch-bad "%s" batch 4096 11 0' % path)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1, result.stderr)
        self.assertIn("verify_failed=json_result.victim.data_errors", result.stderr)

    @unittest.skipUnless(BUSYBOX.is_file(), "busybox not installed")
    def test_int_of_uses_busybox_awk_without_32bit_clamp(self):
        harness = self.temp / "int_of_harness.sh"
        harness.write_text(
            self.harness_prelude
            + "\nprintf '%s\\n' \"$(int_of 4294967295)\" \"$(int_of 0xffffffff)\""
            + " \"$(int_of 64)\" \"$(int_of 0x4)\"\n")
        env = os.environ.copy()
        env["PATH"] = str(self.busybox_bin) + ":" + env.get("PATH", "")
        result = subprocess.run([str(BUSYBOX), "ash", str(harness)], env=env,
                                text=True, capture_output=True, check=False)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout.splitlines(), ["4294967295", "4294967295", "64", "4"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

risks: The new parser tests depend on /usr/bin/busybox for the BusyBox ash+awk path and on a host C compiler plus LD_PRELOAD support. The parser tests fall back to system sh; the numeric BusyBox test is skipped if busybox is absent.

Extracting production shell functions by regex assumes the named functions remain top-level and end with a column-0 closing brace. If the runner is refactored heavily, the extraction helper must be updated.

The before-snapshot batch-time check rejects any matching seq= part=time record in the before snapshot. This is correct for a new startup seq but would fail if the kernel ever emits a pre-run part=time record with the same seq before the batch-start line. The current protocol requires the seq to be new and unique.

The stale-test fixture writes a synthetic stale batch-time line directly into the fake ring. That is a test-only fixture, not a claim about real kernel output; the purpose is to exercise the production absent-before check.
The production parser tests assert acceptance of current stub output. If the stub's default counters or CLI defaults change, update the expected transfers/seq values.
No actual board, DMA, HPM, or FPGA validation is added. These remain host-only checks.
